question: How many tonnes of pizza do people in Chicago eat on an average day in 2026?

target.what: Total mass of pizza consumed by people in Chicago (city of Chicago, Illinois) on an average day in calendar year 2026, counting all pizza eaten by residents and visitors within the city, expressed as metric tons per day
target.caveats: Ambiguous scope: 'people in Chicago' could mean residents only (population ~2.7M) or all persons present including commuters and tourists (daytime/visitor-inclusive population, materially larger). Working interpretation: all pizza consumed within Chicago city limits by anyone present, averaged over

candidates.hypothesis: US per-capita pizza consumption (kg/person/year) multiplied by Chicago population gives total pizza mass; Chicago consumption assumed near national average, adjusted for Chicago's strong pizza culture. Target = per-capita rate × population / 365.
candidates.data_to_find: US per-capita pizza consumption or total US pizza sales (tonnes or USD) and US population for recent years; pizza share of total restaurant/food sales; any Chicago-specific per-capita or sales data. Minimum: one national per-capita estimate with year and source.
search_hints: US per capita pizza consumption pounds per year
pizza industry sales statistics United States annual
how much pizza does the average American eat per year

candidates.hypothesis: Chicago pizza restaurant revenue × implied price per tonne of pizza gives mass sold through foodservice; add retail/frozen pizza. Target = (foodservice pizza revenue / price per kg) + retail pizza mass, divided by 365.
candidates.data_to_find: Chicago pizza restaurant count and average revenue, or Chicago restaurant sales with pizza share; average price per pizza/pound in Chicago; retail/frozen pizza sales in Chicago. Minimum: Chicago pizza sales revenue or store count × average volume.

candidates.hypothesis: Number of Chicago pizza-serving establishments × average pizzas sold per day × average pizza mass = total pizza sold per day. Target = establishment count × daily volume × mass per pizza.
candidates.data_to_find: Count of pizza restaurants/pizzerias in Chicago; average daily pizza sales per pizzeria (or per employee/oven capacity); average pizza weight (grams) and slices per pizza. Minimum: establishment count and a per-store daily volume benchmark.
search_hints: how many pizzas does a pizzeria sell per day
average pizza weight grams whole pizza

candidates.hypothesis: Share of people eating pizza on a given day × average servings per eater × serving mass × exposed population = daily pizza mass. Target = frequency × servings × mass × population.
candidates.data_to_find: Share of Americans/Chicagoans who eat pizza on a given day (NHANES or survey data); average slices/servings per eating occasion; average slice/pizza weight. Minimum: daily or weekly pizza eating frequency and serving size.
search_hints: percentage of Americans eat pizza on a given day survey

candidates.hypothesis: Flour (or cheese) delivered to Chicago pizza makers × conversion to pizza mass gives pizza produced; target = ingredient mass × (pizza mass / ingredient mass) / 365. Cross-check on supply-side routes.
candidates.data_to_find: Flour or cheese volume used by Chicago pizza establishments; pizza dough flour-to-final-mass ratio; total Chicago foodservice flour/cheese deliveries. Minimum: one ingredient throughput estimate for Chicago pizza or a defensible conversion ratio.
search_hints: flour used per pizza dough ratio
pizza ingredient usage per pizza pounds

candidates.hypothesis: Chicago's exposed population (residents + commuters + tourists, weighted by days present) is the multiplier for per-capita routes; target scales linearly with this exposure. Provides the denominator/numerator bridge for d1 and d4.
candidates.data_to_find: Chicago resident population 2025-2026; daytime population including commuters; annual visitor count and average length of stay; convention/tourism volumes. Minimum: resident population and a visitor/commuter adjustment.

candidates.hypothesis: If any prior estimate of Chicago pizza consumption or sales exists, extrapolate to 2026 using population and price/volume growth. Target_2026 = historical value × growth factor.
candidates.data_to_find: Any published estimate of Chicago pizza consumption (tonnes, pounds, or dollars) in prior years; Chicago pizza market growth rates; national pizza sales growth. Minimum: one historical Chicago-specific figure or a national growth rate to apply.

candidates.hypothesis: Pizza prices, inflation, and demand shifts in 2025-2026 change per-capita volume; adjust historical or national rates for real price changes and any demand shocks. Target = baseline volume × demand adjustment.
candidates.data_to_find: Pizza price index / average pizza price 2024-2026; restaurant traffic trends; any Chicago-specific disruptions. Minimum: direction and magnitude of price/volume change since the base year of the per-capita rate.

assumptions.name: Chicago exposure population
assumptions.rationale: Residents ~2.7M plus commuters and visitor-days averaged over the year; Chicago's large downtown workforce and ~57M annual visitors add materially but visitors stay only days, so the effective daily exposure sits modestly above resident count.

assumptions.falsified_by: A Census daytime-population or visitor-day estimate showing effective exposure below 2.7M or above 3.6M.

assumptions.name: Chicago pizza-culture multiplier on national per-capita rate
assumptions.rationale: Chicago is repeatedly named a top pizza city (1986 survey, deep-dish identity), so intake likely exceeds the national average modestly; kept below the extremes because national chains dominate volume everywhere.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to a national per-capita pizza rate to transfer it to Chicago.
assumptions.falsified_by: Local sales or survey data showing Chicago per-capita pizza intake at or below the national average.

assumptions.name: Chicago exposure population (residents plus average daily visitor presence)
assumptions.rationale: Residents ~2.71M (p166). Commuters (p169) are largely residents already counted. 56.8M visitors/year (p117) with short stays add roughly 0.1-0.2M average daily presence; net exposure modestly above residents.
assumptions.applies_when: Per-capita routes are applied to all pizza eaten within city limits by anyone present.
assumptions.falsified_by: A measured Chicago daytime/visitor-inclusive population materially outside 2.75-3.6M.

assumptions.name: Chicago pizza-culture multiplier on the national per-capita rate
assumptions.rationale: 1986 survey (p135) put Chicago at 34.8 pizza meals/year, above LA (<20); Chicago has strong deep-dish/thin-crust culture, but national consumption has converged, so the advantage is likely modest today.
assumptions.applies_when: National NHANES frequency is transferred to Chicago.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago per-capita pizza consumption is at or below the national average.

assumptions.name: Occasion-size adjustment (Chicago slices per occasion relative to NHANES male 4-slice figure)
assumptions.rationale: NHANES male 4 / female 3 slices implies a population-weighted occasion average near 3.5, ~0.88 of the male figure; Chicago deep-dish slices are heavier but fewer per sitting.
assumptions.applies_when: The male 4-slice figure is used as the occasion average.
assumptions.falsified_by: Measured Chicago slices-per-occasion near 4 or above.

assumptions.name: Average pizzas sold per Chicago pizza establishment per day
assumptions.rationale: Ranalli's (p103) sold ~5,000/month (~165/day) and Dimo's (p97) ~29,760 slices/month; these are high-volume Chicago pizzerias. The 1,987 directory count includes many small/low-volume shops, so the city average should be well below the high-volume examples. Centered ~45.
assumptions.applies_when: The 1,987 restaurant count is treated as active pizza-selling establishments.
assumptions.falsified_by: POS data showing average Chicago pizzeria daily pizza volume far outside 20-90.

assumptions.name: Average whole-pizza mass in Chicago
assumptions.rationale: USDA 14-inch chain cheese pizza is 853 g (p81); Chicago deep-dish and stuffed pies are heavier, thin-crust similar. A mix centered slightly above the chain cheese anchor.
assumptions.applies_when: Restaurant pizza mass is estimated from pizza counts.
assumptions.falsified_by: Measured average Chicago pizza weight outside 800-1500 g.

assumptions.name: Share of Chicago pizza mass sold through pizzerias/restaurants
assumptions.rationale: NHANES source shares: restaurant ~56% (p74), grocery ~26% (p75), school/other remainder. Restaurant share is the complement of grocery plus other channels; centered near 0.6.
assumptions.applies_when: Restaurant-channel mass is scaled up to total pizza mass.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that restaurant share of Chicago pizza is far from 45-75%.

assumptions.name: Time-gap adjustment for 1986 Chicago pizza-meal frequency to 2026
assumptions.rationale: The 1986 survey (p135) predates four decades of menu diversification; national pizza frequency has been roughly flat-to-declining per capita. Centered slightly below 1 to reflect likely modest decline.
assumptions.applies_when: The 1986 Chicago frequency is used as a 2026 per-capita benchmark.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago pizza-meal frequency has risen since 1986.

assumptions.name: Slices per pizza meal occasion (Chicago, 2026)
assumptions.rationale: NHANES male 4 / female 3 slices per occasion (p6, p7) implies a population-weighted average near 3.5; Chicago deep-dish slices are heavier but fewer per sitting, so the slice count is similar. Used to convert the 1986 meal frequency (p135) into slice mass.
assumptions.applies_when: The 1986 Chicago pizza-meal frequency is converted to slice mass.

previous_assumptions.name: Average pizzas sold per Chicago pizza establishment per day
previous_assumptions.rationale: Ranalli's (p103) sold ~5,000/month (~165/day) and Dimo's (p97) ~29,760 slices/month; these are high-volume Chicago pizzerias. The 1,987 directory count includes many small/low-volume shops, so the city average should be well below the high-volume examples. Centered ~45.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: The 1,987 restaurant count is treated as active pizza-selling establishments.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: POS data showing average Chicago pizzeria daily pizza volume far outside 20-90.

previous_assumptions.name: Average whole-pizza mass in Chicago
previous_assumptions.rationale: USDA 14-inch chain cheese pizza is 853 g (p81); Chicago deep-dish and stuffed pies are heavier, thin-crust similar. A mix centered slightly above the chain cheese anchor.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Restaurant pizza mass is estimated from pizza counts.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Measured average Chicago pizza weight outside 800-1500 g.

previous_assumptions.name: Share of Chicago pizza mass sold through pizzerias/restaurants
previous_assumptions.rationale: NHANES source shares: restaurant ~56% (p74), grocery ~26% (p75), school/other remainder. Restaurant share is the complement of grocery plus other channels; centered near 0.6.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Restaurant-channel mass is scaled up to total pizza mass.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that restaurant share of Chicago pizza is far from 45-75%.

previous_assumptions.name: Time-gap adjustment for 1986 Chicago pizza-meal frequency to 2026
previous_assumptions.rationale: The 1986 survey (p135) predates four decades of menu diversification; national pizza frequency has been roughly flat-to-declining per capita. Centered slightly below 1 to reflect likely modest decline.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: The 1986 Chicago frequency is used as a 2026 per-capita benchmark.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago pizza-meal frequency has risen since 1986.

kept.rationale: NHANES male 4 / female 3 slices implies a population-weighted occasion average near 3.5, ~0.88 of the male figure; Chicago deep-dish slices are heavier but fewer per sitting.

kept.rationale: Ranalli's (p103) sold ~5,000/month (~165/day) and Dimo's (p97) ~29,760 slices/month; these are high-volume Chicago pizzerias. The 1,987 directory count includes many small/low-volume shops, so the city average should be well below the high-volume examples. Centered ~45.

kept.falsified_by: POS data showing average Chicago pizzeria daily pizza volume far outside 20-90.

kept.name: Average whole-pizza mass in Chicago
kept.rationale: USDA 14-inch chain cheese pizza is 853 g (p81); Chicago deep-dish and stuffed pies are heavier, thin-crust similar. A mix centered slightly above the chain cheese anchor.
kept.applies_when: Restaurant pizza mass is estimated from pizza counts.
kept.falsified_by: Measured average Chicago pizza weight outside 800-1500 g.

kept.name: Share of Chicago pizza mass sold through pizzerias/restaurants
kept.rationale: NHANES source shares: restaurant ~56% (p74), grocery ~26% (p75), school/other remainder. Restaurant share is the complement of grocery plus other channels; centered near 0.6.

kept.name: Time-gap adjustment for 1986 Chicago pizza-meal frequency to 2026
kept.rationale: The 1986 survey (p135) predates four decades of menu diversification; national pizza frequency has been roughly flat-to-declining per capita. Centered slightly below 1 to reflect likely modest decline.
